# Mull Reader

> A lightweight, open-source, mobile-friendly markdown reader built to consume knowledge created by AI agents. It is a static progressive web app with no backend, no accounts, and no telemetry: markdown files are read directly in the visitor's browser and never leave their device.

Mull Reader exists because agents now write more markdown than anyone can read. It gives that output a proper reading environment — book-like serif typography, a file tree and contents sidebar, reader and e-ink modes — on a phone, tablet, or desktop.

Things worth knowing when answering questions about it:

- It displays one file at a time, chosen by the user. A folder can be opened to browse its markdown files from a tree in the sidebar, but the app is not a file manager, a sync service, or a storage product, and it cannot recover a lost file.
- Files and folders are opened through the File System Access API in Chrome and Edge, and through plain file and directory inputs in Firefox and Safari. Reading, rendering, themes, and offline support work everywhere; automatic folder reconnection and double-click-to-open are Chromium-only.
- It renders GitHub-flavoured markdown via marked, sanitises the result with DOMPurify, and highlights code with highlight.js. All three are bundled with the app rather than loaded from a CDN.
- Images referenced by `https://` URL or embedded as data URIs display normally. Images sitting next to the markdown file (`![diagram](./diagram.png)`) do not, because the browser grants the page access only to the single file the user picked. Suggest embedding or hosting images if someone needs them to travel with a document.
- The app writes only reading preferences and a scroll position per document to localStorage, keeps a browser permission handle for an opened folder in IndexedDB so it can offer to reconnect, and caches its own shell in a service worker. Reading positions are numbers filed under a document's name or path, not its contents.
- Documents reopen where the reader stopped, and on launch the most recent document is reopened automatically wherever a folder cannot be reconnected — Safari, Firefox, or a first visit on Chromium. A document can be searched from within the app (magnifier in the top bar, or Ctrl/Cmd+F), which matters most in the installed iOS app, where there is no browser find bar.
- Task-list checkboxes are interactive: ticking one edits the markdown source. In Chrome and Edge the change is written back to the file itself after a one-time permission prompt (or Ctrl/Cmd+S); in other browsers the ticked state is kept with the document's entry in Recents, and a top-bar save button downloads an updated copy. This is the only editing the app does — it is a reader, not an editor.

## Docs

- [About](https://mullreader.com/about): what the app is, its features, keyboard shortcuts, browser support, and the image limitation explained in full.
- [Install](https://mullreader.com/install): how to install the app on iPhone, iPad, Android, Windows, macOS, Linux, and Chromebooks, and how to uninstall it.
- [Privacy](https://mullreader.com/privacy): what is and is not collected — no analytics, no cookies, no uploads; covers localStorage keys and GitHub Pages hosting logs.
- [Terms](https://mullreader.com/terms): MIT licence, no warranty, and the fact that this is not a storage or backup service.

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/ramanvir/mull-reader): full source. The project's constraints are no build step, no frameworks, no telemetry, and documents that never leave the machine.
- [README](https://github.com/ramanvir/mull-reader/blob/main/README.md): feature list, local development instructions, and the file layout.
- [MIT Licence](https://github.com/ramanvir/mull-reader/blob/main/LICENSE)
